summary: The Philippines admits citizens of the countries listed under Executive Order 408 visa-free for 30 days — extendable at a Bureau of Immigration office — and requires arriving travellers, except foreign diplomats, 9(e) visa holders and holders of diplomatic or official passports, to register on the free eTravel platform within 72 hours before arrival. Visa-free visitors must also hold a return or onward ticket.

CN.notes: The Philippine visa policy says Chinese nationals may enter without a visa for a non-extendible and non-convertible period of 14 days for tourism and business, on presenting a passport valid at least six months beyond the intended stay, a confirmed hotel booking and a return or onward ticket, and only through Ninoy Aquino International Airport (Metro Manila) or Mactan-Cebu International Airport (Cebu).

quote.text: Chinese nationals may enter the Philippines without a visa for a non-extendible and non-convertible period of 14 days for tourism and business purposes, subject to the following conditions: Presentation of a passport valid for at least six (6) months beyond the intended stay; Confirmed hotel accommodation or booking; and A return or onward ticket to the next country of destination. Entry under this visa-free privilege shall be allowed only through the following designated ports of entry: Ninoy Aquino International Airport, Metro Manila Mactan-Cebu International Airport, Cebu

onwardTicket.text: The Department of Foreign Affairs' visa policy says visa-free nationals must hold a return ticket to their country of origin or an outward-bound ticket to their next destination. The UK government says immigration officials and airlines may ask for proof of it.

proofOfFunds.text: The Department of Foreign Affairs' visa policy lists proof of financial capacity — such as bank statements for the latest six months or tax payments, an employment certificate with remuneration, proof of business income, or a sponsor's letter of guarantee with proof of financial capacity — among the minimum requirements for a tourism/leisure visitor visa (9(a-2)). It asks Indian nationals entering visa-free for 14 days to show proof of financial capacity. No amount is published.

declarations.name: eTravel Registration
declarations.text: Travellers arriving in the Philippines (foreigners and Filipinos alike), except foreign diplomats and dignitaries, 9(e) visa holders and holders of diplomatic or official passports, must register on the eTravel platform within 72 hours before arrival and present the QR code at check-in and immigration. It is completely free. Use only etravel.gov.ph.

source.name: eTravel — Frequently Asked Questions

currencyLimits.text: Foreign currency over 10,000 USD (or equivalent) must be declared on arrival and departure. Bringing in or taking out more than 50,000 PHP in Philippine currency requires prior authorization from the central bank (BSP).

notes: The UK government says there are strict rules on goods taken into or out of the Philippines, and you must declare anything that may be prohibited or subject to tax or duty.

The Bureau of Customs says all arriving passengers fill in the electronic Customs Baggage Declaration Form (e-CBDF) on the eTravel website or the eGovPH app within 72 hours before arrival, and those carrying currency above the allowed threshold also fill in the electronic Currencies Declaration Form (e-CDF); the eTravel QR code is shown to the customs officer for clearance.

safety.text: The UK Foreign Office advises against all travel to western and central Mindanao and the Sulu archipelago, and against all but essential travel to the rest of Mindanao except Camiguin, Dinagat and Siargao islands, because of terrorist activity and clashes between the military and insurgent groups in the south.

tips.text: Book an onward or return ticket before you fly: the Department of Foreign Affairs says visa-free visitors must hold a return ticket to their country of origin or an outward-bound ticket to their next destination, and the UK government says immigration officials and airlines may ask for it.
Register only on the official eTravel portal, etravel.gov.ph.

After the initial 30 days, the Bureau of Immigration offers a first visa waiver, then further extensions of stay (in 1- or 2-month steps, or up to 6 months under the Long-Stay Visitor Extension); it gives 36 months as the maximum allowable stay for visa-free nationals.

The UK government says around 20 typhoons hit the Philippines each year, mostly between June and November, and Canada says authorities may suspend ferry services at short notice when a storm signal is raised, so you could be stranded at a port for days; Canada advises planning extra time for sea travel, especially in the rainy season.

faq.question: Do US citizens need a visa for the Philippines?
faq.answer: No. US passport holders enter visa-free for up to 30 days with a passport valid 6 months and an onward ticket. The stay can be extended at Bureau of Immigration offices. US citizens must also register on eTravel within 72 hours before arrival.

faq.question: What is eTravel and who needs it?
faq.answer: eTravel (etravel.gov.ph) is the Philippines' free online arrival registration combining immigration, health and customs declarations. Arriving travellers — foreign or Filipino — must complete it, except foreign diplomats and dignitaries, 9(e) visa holders and holders of diplomatic or official passports, within 72 hours before arrival and show the QR code at check-in and on arrival.

faq.question: Is an onward ticket really required for the Philippines?
faq.answer: Yes, for visa-free visitors. The Department of Foreign Affairs' visa policy says visa-free nationals must hold a return ticket to their country of origin or an outward-bound ticket to their next destination. The UK government says immigration officials and airlines may ask for it, and Canada says customs officials may ask to see a return or onward ticket.

faq.question: How do I extend my stay in the Philippines?
faq.answer: Apply at the Bureau of Immigration main office or another authorized immigration office. The first step is a visa waiver (PHP 3,030); after that you can extend in 1- or 2-month steps, or up to 6 months under the Long-Stay Visitor Extension. The Bureau gives 36 months as the maximum allowable stay for visa-free nationals.

faq.question: Do Indian citizens need a visa for the Philippines?
faq.answer: No, not for short visits. Indian passport holders can enter visa-free for 14 days for tourism or business (not extendable), with a passport valid 6 months beyond the stay, a confirmed hotel booking, proof of funds and a return or onward ticket. Those holding a valid US, UK, Schengen, Japanese, Australian, Canadian or Singapore visa or residence permit can instead stay 30 days for tourism, also not extendable. Longer stays need a temporary visitor (9a) visa.
